content: Idiopathic lumbosacral plexopathy (ILSP), also referred to as lumbosacral plexitis or non-diabetic lumbosacral (radiculo)plexus neuropathy, is a rare medical condition. It is characterized by a (sub)acute onset of severe, asymmetrical leg pain, which is followed by asymmetrical, multifocal muscle weakness and atrophy over the course of weeks or months. Sensory symptoms associated with ILSP include paresthesias (abnormal sensations such as tingling or prickling), hypesthesia (reduced sensitivity to touch), allodynia (pain from stimuli that are not normally painful), and autonomic dysfunction. The disease typically follows a monophasic course, meaning it occurs in a single phase and does not relapse. It is self-limiting, with recovery beginning slowly over months to several years, though full recovery is almost never achieved. Some evidence suggests that ILSP may have an immune-mediated origin. Biopsies of distal cutaneous nerve segments in affected individuals have revealed signs of inflammatory microvasculitis, which leads to ischemic damage to the nerves. The clinical and pathological features of ILSP are similar to those observed in diabetic lumbosacral plexus neuropathy, suggesting that inflammation may play a role in the final common pathway of both conditions. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of any form of immunotherapy in the treatment of ILSP. A comprehensive search was conducted on October 15, 2013, across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Neuromuscular Disease Group Specialized Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, EMBASE, LILACS, and Index to Theses. Conference abstracts were reviewed, and trial databases were searched for ongoing studies. References from identified trials were examined, and authors were contacted to identify additional published or unpublished data. The inclusion criteria for the study were as follows: participants had to have an acute or subacute onset of pain and lower motor neuron weakness, predominantly affecting the proximal muscles of the lower limbs. The weakness could not be confined to a single nerve or nerve root distribution. Electrophysiological tests needed to demonstrate predominantly axonal neuropathies. Other causes of lumbosacral radiculopathy and plexopathy had to be excluded, as well as patients with plasma glucose levels in the diabetic range (fasting glucose >7.0 mmol/L or random glucose >11.1 mmol/L). Only randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or quasi-RCTs of any immunotherapy administered within six weeks of disease onset were considered. Two authors independently reviewed all references retrieved during the search to identify studies that met the inclusion criteria, following standard Cochrane methodology. However, no RCTs evaluating the use of immunotherapy for ILSP were identified. In conclusion, there is currently no evidence from randomized trials to support any recommendations regarding the use of immunotherapy for the treatment of ILSP.
